title: The rise of the agentic economy on the shoulders of MCP — Jan Curn, Apify

summary: Jan Curn, Apify founder, opens by drawing analogies between intelligence emerging in biological neurons, markets, companies, and computing systems. In each case, individual entities pursuing self-interest and communicating produce collective intelligence greater than the sum of parts. He argues general intelligence in computing will emerge through interactions among multiple AI agents, not solely from ever-larger models. MCP provides the missing communication layer enabling this agentic mesh. Apify is introduced as a marketplace of 5,000 software tools called actors—self-contained Docker-based units with well-defined inputs and outputs, historically focused on web scraping and data extraction. These integrate via SDKs, workflow automation tools, and now MCP. The killer feature of MCP is tool discovery: clients dynamically discover tools as needed, avoiding context bloat when offering thousands of tools. MCP has become the de facto standard for agentic interaction, with multiple registries emerging. However, a critical gap remains: agents cannot autonomously discover and pay for external services because they still need human developers to provide API tokens and authentication. Curn outlines three solutions: agents subscribing themselves (impractical due to captchas and real-person requirements); centralized identity and payment providers like Coinbase X42 or Stripe (promising but facing marketplace chicken-and-egg challenges); and a decentralized marketplace model like Apify's, where developers wrap external services with their own credentials and monetization. MCP server nesting allows a parent server to expose nested MCP servers' tools, enabling rapid ecosystem scaling even without target services' awareness. The demo shows Claude for desktop with 18 available Apify MCP tools answering a venue question via the rag-web-browser actor, then dynamically discovering a Twitter scraper actor, adding it to context, and retrieving the latest tweet from the AI Engineer conference. A second demo shows Apify wrapping Browserbase's MCP server—creating an account, adding their own API token, and publishing it on the Apify store without Browserbase's knowledge—then using it to fill an email subscription form on the AI Engineer website. This demonstrates how MCP server nesting can rapidly expand the ecosystem without third-party cooperation. Curn reports Apify paid over $4 million to creators last month, actors generate more than $500,000 per month, and the ecosystem sees 1 million monthly visitors. He closes with open questions: whether autonomous tool discovery will provide reliable value, how agents can establish trust with tools and each other, and whether autonomous agent interaction can enable AGI.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Emergence of Intelligence
sections.summary: Curn draws analogies between intelligence emerging in biological neurons, markets, companies, and computing systems, arguing AGI will emerge from interacting agents enabled by MCP.

sections.title: Apify and the Agentic Economy
sections.summary: Introduction to Apify as a marketplace of 5,000 Docker-based tools called actors, now accessible via MCP. Tool discovery is highlighted as the killer feature differentiating MCP from OpenAPI, avoiding context bloat with thousands of tools.

sections.title: Challenges and Solutions for Agent Autonomy
sections.summary: Agents cannot autonomously discover and pay for external services due to API token dependency. Three solutions discussed: self-subscription (impractical), centralized payment providers (slow to establish), and decentralized marketplace with MCP server nesting (scalable, no target service awareness needed).

sections.title: Demo of Apify's MCP Integration
sections.summary: Pre-recorded demos: Claude for desktop uses Apify MCP server with 18 tools to answer a venue question via rag-web-browser; dynamically discovers and adds a Twitter scraper actor to retrieve the latest AI Engineer conference tweet; uses Browserbase MCP server (published by Apify with their own API token, without Browserbase's knowledge) to fill an email subscription form, demonstrating MCP server nesting for ecosystem expansion without third-party cooperation.

sections.title: Monetization and Future Outlook
sections.summary: Curn reports Apify paid over $4 million to creators last month, actors generate over $500K/month, with 1 million monthly visitors. He invites developers to publish tools on Apify for monetization. He closes with open questions: whether autonomous tool discovery will provide reliable value, how agents can trust tools and each other, and whether autonomous agent interaction can enable AGI.
